Remark. Clausen function \mathrm{Cl}_2 as repo-internal Mathlib filler

Remark (Clausen function Cl_2 as repo-internal Mathlib filler).

Mathlib lacks the Clausen function

  \mathrm{Cl}_2(\theta)
  \;:=\;
  \sum_{k = 1}^\infty \frac{\sin(k\theta)}{k^2}
  \;=\; \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(e^{i\theta}).

This function evaluates the imaginary part of the dilogarithm on the unit circle. It dictates standard hyperbolic volume formulas:

  \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)\;=\;2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3)\;\approx\;2.02988,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)\;=\;8\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/4)\;=\;8G\;\approx\;7.327724.

The Lean library file QOU/Archimedean/ClausenFunctionMathlibFiller.lean provides the Cl_2 series definition and the boundary/volume carriers; the integral-side definition, the derivative Cl_2'(\theta) = -\log(2\sin(\theta/2)), and the series–integral bridge (the classical Zagier identity) are machine-proved in QOU/Knot/Clausen.lean (fundamental theorem of calculus plus an Abel-regularised assembly). Building on this infrastructure, the figure-eight case of the Kashaev volume conjecture — the limit (2\pi/N)\log\langle 4_1\rangle_N \to 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3) = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) — is itself machine-proved, sorry-free, in QOU/Knot/FigureEightVolumeSqueeze.lean by a Riemann-sum squeeze of the Kashaev log-sum against the Clausen primitive, with the exact transcendental target \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2\,\mathrm{Cl}_2(\pi/3).

This construction unconditionalizes the Bloch-Wigner values in the \alpha_{\text{EM}} chain. Explicit Lean carriers replace opaque references. The framework references \mathrm{Cl}_2, \mathrm{Vol}(4_1), and \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) via these carriers in em-coupling-bring-zero-mode, figure-8-archimedean-illustration, bring-hyperbolic-knot-bloch-decomposition, and binding-scale-catalan.

Mathlib gaps

See Table 2.

Six conditional classes remain as mathematical infrastructure gaps: BlochSuslinUniqueness, ArchimedeanLimit, BringZeroModeBlochClass, BringHyperbolicDecomposition, BWQIndependence, and BlochWignerInjective. Closing these classes requires upstream Mathlib contributions or internal formalization.

Pattern

Each Mathlib gap forms a scoped task. The \mathrm{Cl}_2 filler defines a single function as a tsum. It provides two unconditional boundary lemmas. Four sketched extensions require Fourier-series infrastructure. This pattern extends to:

  • A Real.dilog filler extending LiTwo to the complex domain via Complex.dilog.
  • A BlochGroup F filler constructing the free abelian group quotient by 5-term pentagon relations.

This file isolates the \mathrm{Cl}_2 filler to support the \alpha_{\text{EM}} and figure-8 chains.
